what: Draws the 3D object (two commas extruded to thickness 46 and stood facing front) on a 2× panel of cols×rows cells with white Phong material and three lights, and sets each cell’s brightness as ” .',:;Swap to one character from Il!i+?][1)(|tfjrxnuvczXYUJCLQ0OZmwqpdbkhao*#MW&8%B@$」 <pre> …stamped there — the lettering image turns its head by its distance from the cell center to the cursor (±.78rad horizontal, ±.42rad vertical), and while following it closes 1 − .001^dt of the gap per frame. With no cursor it sways slowly at .55 beats per second by ±.22 and ±.08rad. With follow: drag it instead sways by itself ±.38rad, and when dragged it turns .01rad per 1px

options.cols: Number of character cells across, default 98 (original CTA 146)
options.rows: Number of text cell rows, default 45 (original CTA 68)
options.scale: Pixel multiplier for drawing one cell, default 2
options.yaw: Max horizontal rotation angle following the cursor (rad), default .78
options.follow: If drag, drag to rotate instead of using the cursor

note: three is read as window.THREE (three.cjs from _vendor/three@0.184.0 is received as window.exports and copied onto THREE). The original read a hidden WebGL panel with readPixels. Here the drawn panel is copied onto a 2D canvas (willReadFrequently) and read from there, to avoid the GPU stall warning in the Chrome console. Text size is kept at 6px and only scaled down with transform scale to fit the panel. It does not draw while off-screen.
